batch:
Survey's done and Batch 1 is ready for your approval. I haven't changed or recorded anything yet.

## Estate now

| Kind | Count | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Rules | 80 active (57 obligation, 23 prod-only), T-81 to T-85 already retired | `register.md` 6 KB |
| Obligations | 59 entries: 56 active, I-55 waived, I-56 deferred, I-58 split parent | `obligations.json` 61 KB, rendered 57 KB |
| Ledger | 39 entries | 2.7 KB |
| Open debt | 15, all kept once | 6.7 KB rendered |

`arc-next` already omits I-54 and C-39, so neither needs a decision. If you approve all three batches, I estimate about 24 rules, 20 obligation entries, 15 ledger lines and no open debt.

## Problems compaction can't fix

- **Missing witness tests:** the test file has three tests (`list`, `I-20`, `cancelled exports`), and all three pass. Of the 58 witnessed obligations, only I-20 names a test that exists. The executor doesn't count a missing test as holding the property, so every "Gives up: nothing" below means the demand survives, not that it's proven. This needs root adjudication in the next arc.
- **Unbuilt behavior:** the source has no date validation, audit trail, sessions, locks, archive, tokens or dispatch. The rules for these stay as demands the product doesn't meet yet.
- **V-2 coverage:** no obligation cites V-2, your non-negotiable integrity clause. All of them, including I-20, serve V-1 only.

## Keeping as they are

- **T-20, I-20 and C-34:** these are the integrity boundary F-1 and F-2 violated. C-34 repeats T-20, but it also records why the rule matters.
- **T-21 and I-21:** the next slice depends on them.
- **T-54, T-55 and T-56:** merging these sort rules would revive I-54 and erase the return conditions on I-55 and I-56.
- **C-30, C-31 and C-32:** these record the dispositions behind those three obligations.
- **T-57 and T-58:** T-58 carries the I-58 split family.

## Batch 1: rules

1. retire T-8
   - Items: T-8 "The PortLink SOAP bridge retries failed deliveries every ten minutes." and I-8.
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: the ten-minute retry demand on a bridge that no longer exists.
   - Why: the previous arc removed the bridge, and `src/` has no trace of it. B-2 follows in Batch 2.

2. retire T-33
   - Items: T-33 "Dispatch is allowed until 72 hours before the tide (working assumption P-1)." and I-33.
   - Replacement: none. T-72 "Dispatch is allowed until 48 hours before the tide." stays, and P-1's `bears` moves from T-33 to T-72.
   - Gives up: the 72-hour assumption and I-33, the only obligation on the dispatch cutoff.
   - Why: you answered P-1 with 48 hours.
   - T-72 is prod-only, so no test will demand any cutoff after this. I'd still retire T-33, because it demands the wrong number.

3. merge T-27 into T-41
   - Items: T-27 "The export command refuses invalid dates." and I-27, into T-41 "Every command refuses invalid dates before reading or writing records."
   - Replacement: T-41, text unchanged. I-41's witness gains test id `I-27`, with a fresh proof judgment.
   - Gives up: nothing. T-41 covers export and is stricter about timing.
   - Why: T-27 is a narrower copy of T-41.

4. merge T-14 into T-3
   - Items: T-14 "No two entries in the register have the same berth booking identifier." and I-14, into T-3 "A berth booking identifier is unique across the register."
   - Replacement: T-3, text unchanged. I-3's witness gains test id `I-14`, with a fresh proof judgment.
   - Gives up: nothing. Both rules ban the same state.
   - Why: they are duplicates.

5. tighten T-49
   - Items: T-49 "In order to ensure that the operator can rely on the output when things go wrong, every failed command, without exception, prints its diagnostic to stderr rather than to stdout."
   - Replacement: T-49 "Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, not stdout." `register.md` prose gains "Failed commands keep diagnostics off stdout so the operator can rely on the output when things go wrong." I-49 moves to rev 2 with a fresh proof judgment.
   - Gives up: nothing. "Every" carries "without exception", and the purpose moves to the prose.
   - Why: same demand in fewer words.

6. retire T-52
   - Items: T-52 "Comment text is grammatical English." and I-52 "One internal comment is grammatical English."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: any grammar demand on comments.
   - Why: it serves neither vision clause. I-52 has also drifted weaker than its rule, and fixing that isn't worth a test.

7. retire T-62
   - Items: T-62 "Internal local variable names use lower camel case."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: the naming demand. The code can drift from camel case without a rule catching it.
   - Why: it is style with no effect on the operator, and it's already prod-only.

8. retire T-63
   - Items: T-63 "The command must be implemented in executable program instructions."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: nothing in practice, since a command that runs already meets it.
   - Why: it rules nothing out.

9. retire T-70
   - Items: T-70 "The welcome banner ends with a period."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: banner punctuation, if a banner is ever added.
   - Why: the product has no welcome banner.

10. retire T-5, T-6 and T-9
    - Items: T-5 "The list command rejects a missing record id with exit 2." and I-5; T-6 "The export command rejects a missing record id with exit 2." and I-6; T-9 "The reserve command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage." and I-9.
    - Replacement: none
    - Gives up: those three refusals, which the product deliberately doesn't make.
    - Why: each contradicts the product, which is my reading rather than something the check-in says.
    - T-5: `list` takes no id, and the `list` test requires it to succeed without one (`src/cli.js:10`).
    - T-6: the `export` argument is a format that defaults to JSON (`src/cli.js:11`).
    - T-9: `reserve` with a new id is how a booking gets created (`src/cli.js:20`), so T-9 would block the main V-1 flow.

## Still to come

- **Batch 2, debt and ledger:**
  - Resolve B-2 and the duplicate B-6.
  - Resolve the record and audit index debt, since each command parses a whole local JSON file anyway.
  - Resolve B-11.
  - Retire C-23 and C-38, and remove C-38's citation from `slips.json`.
  - Fold C-4 and C-12 + C-17 into the corpus.
- **Batch 3, command families:**
  - Merge the per-command rules and ledger entries, naming the exact commands so nothing widens.
  - Absorb T-65 to T-69 and T-71 into T-41.
  - Collapse T-73 to T-80, the only family that covers all eight commands, into one rule.

Which of 1 to 10 do you approve? "All" works, or name any you want changed or dropped. Approved decisions go to `../roadmap-inputs/drafts/compaction.md` straight away, and then I'll bring Batch 2.
reply:
1: approve
2: approve
3: approve
4: approve
5: approve, with this exact wording instead: "Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, never stdout."
6: reject as proposed. Retire I-52 only, with no replacement; T-52 stays. Accepted loss: a separate test demanding grammatical English in one internal comment.
7: approve
8: approve
9: reject. Keep T-70.
10: reject. Keep T-5, T-6, T-9, I-5, I-6 and I-9.

K-1 to K-8 are recorded in `../roadmap-inputs/drafts/compaction.md`. Batch 1 retires T-8, T-33, T-27, T-14, T-62 and T-63, which takes rules from 80 to 74. It removes I-8, I-33, I-27, I-14 and I-52, which takes obligation entries from 59 to 54.

## Batch 2: debt and ledger

The K and C ids below assume you approve all nine, and I'll play back any that shift. New ledger entries start at C-41. Ledger lines are quoted exactly, so they keep the format's em dash.

1. resolve B-2
   - Items: B-2 "Remove the retry queue in the PortLink SOAP bridge."
   - Replacement: `C-41 — B-2 resolved by compaction K-9: the bridge is gone; retry-queue cleanup is given up.`
   - Gives up: retry-queue cleanup in the removed bridge.
   - Why: the bridge left the product in the previous arc.

2. resolve B-6
   - Items: B-6 "Index reserve record lookup; B-1 already tracks the same index."
   - Replacement: `C-42 — B-6 resolved by compaction K-10: B-1 tracks the same reserve record-lookup index; nothing is given up.`
   - Gives up: nothing.
   - Why: B-6 says itself that it duplicates B-1.

3. resolve B-1, B-3, B-4, B-5, B-7 and B-8
   - Items: "Add an index for `<command>` record lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call." for reserve (B-1), arrive (B-3), depart (B-4), list (B-5), inspect (B-7) and search (B-8).
   - Replacement: `C-43 — B-1, B-3, B-4, B-5, B-7 and B-8 resolved by compaction K-11: each command parses the whole local register file, so an index saves no meaningful work; record lookups stay linear scans.`
   - Gives up: indexed record lookup for those six commands.
   - Why: `src/cli.js:8` reads and parses the whole file on every call, so an index would have to be rebuilt each time or stored separately.

4. resolve B-9, B-10, B-12, B-13, B-14 and B-15
   - Items: "Add an index for `<command>` audit lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call." for reserve (B-9), cancel (B-10), depart (B-12), list (B-13), export (B-14) and inspect (B-15).
   - Replacement: `C-44 — B-9, B-10, B-12, B-13, B-14 and B-15 resolved by compaction K-12: the product has no audit trail to index; audit-lookup indexes are given up.`
   - Gives up: the planned audit-lookup indexes for those six commands.
   - Why: nothing writes an audit trail yet. T-42 to T-48 still demand one, and an index can come back as new debt once it exists and proves slow.

5. resolve B-11
   - Items: B-11 "Align the success message punctuation with the help footer."
   - Replacement: `C-45 — B-11 resolved by compaction K-13: the product has no help footer and mutating commands print only the record id; the punctuation alignment is given up.`
   - Gives up: the punctuation alignment.
   - Why: there's nothing to align with, since the CLI only has a usage error line.
   - You kept T-70, which is also about punctuation, so this may be one you'd rather keep too.

6. retire C-23
   - Items: `C-23 — The first release demo uses the blue harbour slide template.`
   - Replacement: none. The line is removed.
   - Gives up: the slide template requirement for that demo.
   - Why: nothing in the product or inputs depends on it, and the cut line says the previous release is complete.
   - I can't confirm from the repo that the demo has happened. Reject this if it's still coming.

7. retire C-38
   - Items: `C-38 — Temporary trace output is permitted for this arc only.`
   - Replacement: none. The line is removed, along with C-38 in `slips.json` `cites.rulings`. C-40 "Trace output redacts operator credentials." stays.
   - Gives up: the permission for temporary trace output. Adding trace output later would need a new ruling.
   - Why: the arc it covered is complete, `src/` has no trace output, and the next arc's slip spec shouldn't carry the expired permission.

8. fold C-4
   - Items: `C-4 — The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision.`
   - Replacement: T-? "The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision." The C-4 line is removed, and the new rule's census state is `out-of-slice`.
   - Gives up: nothing. The text is verbatim, and C-4 had no witness to lose.
   - Why: your check-in calls this a standing truth, but workers never see the ledger, so it can't reach them as a C-n.
   - The product has no archive yet, so this moves the demand without delivering it.

9. fold C-12 and C-17
   - Items: `C-12 — A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response.` and `C-17 — Retries with the same request token return the stored response without another mutation.`
   - Replacement: T-? "A request token is accepted once; retries with the same token return the stored response without another mutation." Both lines are removed, along with C-12 in `slips.json` `cites.rulings`, and the new rule's census state is `out-of-slice`.
   - Gives up: nothing. I checked four properties against the new text: accepted once, retries return the stored response, retries match on the same token, and no second mutation.
   - Why: same reason as C-4, and it also removes the overlap between the two entries.
   - The product has no tokens yet. Together with decision 7, this leaves the slip spec citing no rulings, which the spec format allows.

Which of 1 to 9 do you approve?
reply:
1: approve
2: approve
3: reject
4: reject
5: approve; T-70 stays
6: approve
7: reject; C-38 stays, including in `slips.json` `cites.rulings`
8: approve
9: approve, with this exact wording instead: "A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response without another mutation."

Play back the shifted K and C ids and the wording for 9.

K-9 to K-14 are recorded. The running totals are 76 rules, 54 obligation entries, 38 ledger lines and 12 open debts.

## Batch 3: command families

These merges replace per-command rules with one rule naming the same commands. Three things apply to all of them:

- **No widening:** each rule names exactly the commands it covers today, so existing gaps stay gaps. Closing one would be a new demand, not compaction.
- **Your earlier calls stand:** you kept T-5, T-6 and T-9, so they stay as separate rules outside decisions 1 and 2. T-54 to T-58 stay out too, as I said in Batch 1.
- **Obligations:** where the old rules had obligations, one new must-hold obligation with a new id (I-61 upward) replaces them. It serves V-1, its witness lists all the old test ids, and it needs a fresh proof judgment.

There's one real cost, which doesn't appear under "Gives up" because no demand is lost. If one command breaks a merged rule, the whole obligation goes red, and the failing test id is what tells you which command it was.

1. merge T-1, T-2, T-4 and T-7
   - Items: "The `<command>` command rejects a missing record id with exit 2." for reserve (T-1, I-1), cancel (T-2, I-2), depart (T-4, I-4) and inspect (T-7, I-7).
   - Replacement: T-? "The reserve, cancel, depart and inspect commands reject a missing record id with exit 2."
   - Gives up: nothing. All four commands, the refusal and exit 2 are all named.
   - Why: same claim four times.

2. merge T-10, T-11, T-12, T-13, T-15 and T-16
   - Items: "The `<command>` command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage." for cancel (T-10, I-10), arrive (T-11, I-11), depart (T-12, I-12), list (T-13, I-13), inspect (T-15, I-15) and search (T-16, I-16).
   - Replacement: T-? "The cancel, arrive, depart, list, inspect and search commands reject an unknown record id without writing storage."
   - Gives up: nothing. All six commands, the refusal and no write are all named.
   - Why: same claim six times.

3. merge T-17, T-18, T-19, T-22, T-23 and T-24
   - Items: "The `<command>` command prints the record id on successful completion." for reserve (T-17, I-17), cancel (T-18, I-18), arrive (T-19, I-19), export (T-22, I-22), inspect (T-23, I-23) and search (T-24, I-24).
   - Replacement: T-? "The reserve, cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search commands print the record id on successful completion."
   - Gives up: nothing. All six commands are named.
   - Why: same claim six times.

4. merge T-25, T-26, T-28, T-29, T-30, T-31 and T-32
   - Items: "The `<command>` command refuses a record belonging to another operator." for reserve (T-25, I-25), cancel (T-26, I-26), depart (T-28, I-28), list (T-29, I-29), export (T-30, I-30), inspect (T-31, I-31) and search (T-32, I-32).
   - Replacement: T-? "The reserve, cancel, depart, list, export, inspect and search commands refuse a record belonging to another operator."
   - Gives up: nothing. All seven commands are named.
   - Why: same claim seven times.

5. merge T-34, T-35, T-38, T-39 and T-40
   - Items: "The `<command>` command preserves the creation timestamp." for cancel (T-34, I-34), arrive (T-35, I-35), export (T-38, I-38), inspect (T-39, I-39) and search (T-40, I-40).
   - Replacement: T-? "The cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search commands preserve the creation timestamp."
   - Gives up: nothing. All five commands are named.
   - Why: same claim five times.

6. merge T-42, T-43, T-44, T-45, T-46, T-47 and T-48
   - Items: "The `<command>` command records the operator in the audit trail." for cancel (T-42, I-42), arrive (T-43, I-43), depart (T-44, I-44), list (T-45, I-45), export (T-46, I-46), inspect (T-47, I-47) and search (T-48, I-48).
   - Replacement: T-? "The cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect and search commands record the operator in the audit trail."
   - Gives up: nothing. All seven commands are named.
   - Why: same claim seven times.

7. merge T-50, T-51 and T-53
   - Items: "The `<command>` command sorts multiple matching records by creation time." for cancel (T-50, I-50), arrive (T-51, I-51) and list (T-53, I-53).
   - Replacement: T-? "The cancel, arrive and list commands sort multiple matching records by creation time."
   - Gives up: nothing. All three commands are named.
   - Why: same claim three times. T-54, T-55 and T-56 stay separate, so I-54 stays retired, I-55 stays waived and I-56 stays deferred.

8. merge T-59, T-60, T-61 and T-64
   - Items: "The `<command>` command returns exit 0 for an empty result." for arrive (T-59), depart (T-60), list (T-61) and search (T-64). All four are prod-only.
   - Replacement: T-? "The arrive, depart, list and search commands return exit 0 for an empty result." Its census state stays prod-only, and it needs no obligation.
   - Gives up: nothing. All four commands are named.
   - Why: same claim four times. T-57 and T-58 stay separate because they carry obligations and the I-58 split family.

9. merge T-65, T-66, T-67, T-68, T-69 and T-71 into T-41

10. merge T-73 to T-80

    - Replacement: T-? "Every command leaves the previous file intact when a write fails." Its census state stays prod-only, and it needs no obligation.
    - Gives up: nothing today, since these are all eight commands in `src/cli.js:3`. "Every" would also cover any command added later, which I think is what you'd want.
    - Why: it's the only family with no gaps. The code already writes to a pending file and renames it (`src/cli.js:30`).

If you approve all ten, that's 29 rules and 23 obligation entries. Batch 4 is the last one, merging the five per-command ledger families (C-1, C-9, C-18, C-25 and C-33).

Which of 1 to 10 do you approve?
